meta.title: About Alan Belferrag | HPC and Cloud Infrastructure
meta.description: I’m Alan Belferrag, an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer. I consult independently on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC.

hero.description: I’m Alan Belferrag, an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer and a Research Computing Specialist at a university. I also consult independently on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC. My projects include RGCP, a self-service GPU compute bridge, and the design of ACC, an Azure HPC platform.

whatYouGet.heading: Selected infrastructure work
whatYouGet.lead: RGCP covers GPU infrastructure and cost governance. ParallelCluster and ACC cover AWS delivery and Azure HPC design. Spack Stack covers scientific software governance across HPC systems. Each case study outlines my role and the project's constraints.

principles.heading: Design around the workload
principles.lead: I design platforms around how they’ll be operated, the workloads they’ll run, and their cost limits.

items.title: Fit the operating model
items.description: Choose orchestration and automation that the team has the capacity to operate.

items.title: Fit the workload mix
items.description: Plan for tightly coupled MPI jobs and memory-heavy, single-node workloads when shaping the cluster and scheduler policy.

items.title: Plan for cost limits
items.description: Use capacity planning and visible usage controls to keep cloud compute within budget.

stack.title: HPC and cloud infrastructure
stack.description: My project work includes Azure CycleCloud, Slurm, MPI, Spack, Lmod, HyperStack, and cloud cluster design for research workloads.

faq.heading: Questions about my consulting work
faq.lead: A few details about my services and how I work.

items.question: What does the GPU cost-reduction offer cover?
items.answer: I review GPU and model-serving costs, find ways to reduce GPU or token spend, and help put changes in place. We agree on the scope and savings baseline before each engagement.

items.question: Is there an upfront fee for this offer?
items.answer: There’s no upfront fee. You pay only after I demonstrate real savings.

items.question: How do you measure savings?
items.answer: Before work starts, we agree on the cost baseline, comparison period, and how to verify savings. The method depends on the workloads and scope.

items.question: What GPU work have you done?
items.answer: The RGCP case study describes a self-service GPU compute platform with cost governance.

items.question: What kind of cloud HPC work do you take on?
items.answer: Cluster and cloud-compute planning and design for research-oriented organizations, including Slurm-based environments on platforms such as AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.

items.question: What HPC work have you done?
items.answer: The ACC case study describes my Azure HPC platform design work.

items.question: Who would I work with?
items.answer: I work independently and directly with clients. This consulting activity is separate from my day job in university research computing.

items.question: Where are you available to work?
items.answer: I’m based in Qatar and travel frequently in France/Europe. I’m also open to remote work with clients elsewhere.

openSource.heading: Work with me directly
openSource.description: I work directly with clients through my independent consulting practice.

meta.title: HPC and GPU infrastructure consulting | Alan Belferrag
meta.description: GPU infrastructure and cost reduction for AI teams, with payment tied to demonstrated savings. Cloud HPC consulting for research and engineering organizations.

hero.description: I help AI teams reduce GPU and token costs, and help research and engineering organizations plan cloud HPC environments.

design.heading: GPU cost reduction for AI teams
paragraphs: As AI workloads grow, GPU capacity and model-serving costs can be harder to track. I review compute use, find ways to reduce GPU and token spend, and help put changes in place.
There’s no upfront fee. You pay only after I demonstrate real savings. The RGCP case study covers my work on self-service GPU compute and cost governance.

included.text: review GPU and model-serving usage and agree on a cost baseline.
identify changes that could reduce GPU or token spend while taking workload needs into account.
agree on how to compare costs, apply the changes, and measure savings.

included.lead: No upfront fee for this offer
included.text: payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings.
see RGCP for an example of GPU compute provisioning and cost governance.

development.heading: Cloud HPC consulting
paragraphs: I help research and engineering teams plan cloud compute around their workloads, operational capacity, security requirements, and budget. This includes Slurm platforms on AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.
The ACC case study covers my Azure CycleCloud-managed Slurm platform design, including scheduling, storage, identity, budget controls, and scientific software environments.

included.text: design the cloud HPC platform and operating model around the organization’s needs.
consider multi-node MPI and memory-heavy single-node jobs in the Slurm design.
plan shared research storage and centrally managed scientific software where required.
account for institutional access, identity requirements, capacity limits, and cost controls.
see ACC for an example of Azure cloud HPC platform design.

performance.heading: Cost controls for compute platforms
paragraphs: Clear usage limits and visibility help prevent unplanned cloud spend. I include capacity and cost controls in the infrastructure design.
The right measures depend on the workload and operating model. RGCP and ACC show how usage limits, capacity planning, and scale-to-zero can work in different compute environments.

included.text: make compute use visible to the people responsible for cost and capacity.
consider enforceable usage limits or project budgets where appropriate.
match capacity decisions to the workload, project constraints, and expected use.
consider autoscaling or scale-to-zero for temporary and variable workloads.
for the GPU cost-reduction offer, you pay only after I demonstrate savings.

steps.title: Set constraints
steps.description: Clarify technical, operational, security, and cost constraints that shape the possible approach.

steps.title: Agree scope and measures

items.answer: I work with research organizations and engineering teams running scientific or simulation workloads.
